comments.note: CacheableAPIMethodTrait::getCacheFile() is declared protected, which is consistent with CacheableAPIMethodInterface not including it (it's an internal helper). However, test code that wants to verify the cache file path must either make it accessible via a stub or use the public getCacheKey() method. This is by design but worth noting for future test authoring.

The trait uses serialize() on the parameters array for cache key generation. This produces a non-human-readable key component. If debugging cached files on disk becomes important, using json_encode() instead would make the hash input more readable in debug logs. Both are deterministic; serialize() handles all PHP types (including nested arrays/objects) more robustly.

CacheableAPIMethodTrait assumes $this->getMethodName() is available via APIMethodInterface. If the trait is ever used outside an APIMethodInterface implementation (e.g., in a test double that does not extend BaseAPIMethod), getMethodName() will be missing. The interface + trait contract is correctly documented in the class docblock, but a @template or static analysis annotation could help IDEs enforce this.

No dedicated unit tests exist for CacheableAPIMethodInterface or CacheableAPIMethodTrait. Tests should be added once the vendor environment is restored (composer install). The plan specifies tests in tests/AppFrameworkTests/API/Cache/.

comments.note: getCacheKey() uses md5() for hashing. The WP spec lists md5 as acceptable, but sha256 (or hash('sha256', ...)) would be more collision-resistant with negligible performance difference. Not a defect; a forward-looking improvement.

No PHPUnit tests for CacheableAPIMethodInterface or CacheableAPIMethodTrait. The Developer acknowledged this and noted tests should be added once vendor is restored. Tests should cover: (1) getCacheKey() determinism with same/different inputs, (2) readFromCache() null on missing file, (3) readFromCache() null on expired strategy, (4) readFromCache() returns parsed array on valid file, (5) writeToCache() persists data to correct path, (6) invalidateCache() delegates to APICacheManager. Suggested location: tests/AppFrameworkTests/API/Cache/.

getCacheKeyParameters() values containing PHP objects are serialized with serialize(), which may produce different byte strings for equivalent logical states (e.g., private property order after clone). The WP spec intends scalar parameter values (name=>value pairs), so this is an expected-use-only boundary. A docblock note on getCacheKeyParameters() warning callers to use scalars only would prevent misuse.

readFromCache() propagates JSONConverterException if the cache file contains malformed JSON. No error handling is present. This is consistent with framework convention (let exceptions propagate), but callers should be aware that a corrupted cache file will surface as an unhandled exception rather than a cache miss. Consider whether APICacheManager::invalidateMethod() should be called as recovery in a higher-level wrapper.
No observations — all core logic is clean, well-structured, and consistent with project conventions. The interface/trait split is idiomatic for this codebase.

summary: WP-003 PASS. CacheableAPIMethodInterface and CacheableAPIMethodTrait reviewed line-by-line against all four Review Dimensions.

Interface: contract is accurate, extends APIMethodInterface correctly (guaranteeing getMethodName() via inheritance), all 6 method signatures match the plan spec, docblocks are clear and include @see cross-references.

Trait: getCacheKey() ksort()+serialize() determinism is correct; getCacheFile() path construction is framework-idiomatic (FolderInfo, JSONFile, forward slashes); readFromCache() guard logic is correct (exists + strategy validity before parse()); writeToCache() and invalidateCache() are correctly thin delegations.

Security: md5() is used for cache filename derivation only — not cryptographic, no concern. Path construction uses getMethodName() from hardcoded implementations, not user input — no path traversal risk.
Conventions: declare(strict_types=1), array() syntax, namespace Application\API\Cache, no raw file ops — all correct.
No blocking issues found. Four non-blocking suggestions recorded as comments.

comments.note: CacheableAPIMethodTrait: readFromCache() can propagate JSONConverterException from JSONFile::parse() if the cache file contains malformed JSON. This is framework-idiomatic (let exceptions bubble), but neither the interface nor the trait has a @throws docblock to document this propagation. A caller that assumes null-on-all-failures will be surprised. Adding @throws JSONConverterException to both the interface and trait signatures would document the boundary accurately.

CacheableAPIMethodInterface::getCacheKeyParameters() docblock should add an explicit warning that parameter values must be scalar. serialize() on PHP objects may produce different byte strings for logically equivalent states (e.g., after clone or across PHP versions), breaking cache key determinism. A single docblock sentence — e.g., 'Values should be scalar types to ensure deterministic serialization' — would prevent misuse.

CacheableAPIMethodTrait: consider adding @phpstan-require-implements CacheableAPIMethodInterface as a trait-level PHPDoc annotation. This lets PHPStan statically enforce that the trait is never used without the interface (which provides getCacheKeyParameters() and getMethodName()), eliminating the runtime-only contract assumption. No code change required — a single annotation at the top of the trait.

getCacheKey() uses md5() for hash generation. For a cache filename key this is functionally fine — md5 is not used for cryptographic integrity here. However, hash('sha256', ...) is a minimal change that eliminates any theoretical collision concern as the cache grows large (many methods × many version × many param combinations). Low priority; not a defect.
